transcript.content: Extend this existing SVG board renderer with a user-selected fill color. Its current label output and tests must keep working.
Source offer offer-89d39751-1141-4980-a73b-87dd1efed86a: How should the user-selected fill color be accepted while keeping the existing label output unchanged?

sourceOffers.scope: Extend the existing SVG board renderer with a user-selected fill color; existing label output and tests keep working, delta only, no rewrite
sourceOffers.question: How should the user-selected fill color be accepted while keeping the existing label output unchanged?

options.label: Optional second fill argument, default preserves output
options.tradeoff: Smallest delta on the existing render signature, but positional args scale poorly if more styling is added later.
options.acceptanceExample: Given existing call render('A'), when run, then it still returns '<text>A</text>'; given render('A', 'red'), then label A is preserved with fill red applied.

options.label: Additive fill that keeps the existing test green
options.tradeoff: Guarantees backward compatibility for the label case, but leaves fill validation and defaults to be decided.
options.acceptanceExample: Given existing test render('A') equals '<text>A</text>', when the fill delta lands, then that test still passes unchanged and render('A', 'red') adds only the fill.

options.label: Fill-color delta only, label behavior untouched
options.tradeoff: Limits the slice to the documented gap, but defers any broader renderer redesign.
options.acceptanceExample: Given the limitation that labels work but fill is missing, when a fill is selected, then labels render exactly as before plus the chosen fill.

source.quote: Current renderer supports labels but not a user-selected fill color. Preserve its existing label output.
